That is the qualified-name and method-ownership adjustment the request asks about. The blocks come from radon/visitors.py: visit_FunctionDef (line 268) collects closures, and visit_ClassDef (line 297) collects inner_classes. Treat that as a cheap check that they don't touch block flattening, not as a finding that they matter. A grep for closures/inner_classes found nothing in either file. If the review has to follow the evidence, B and D deserve most of the time. Points to check: (1) `all_blocks.pop()` takes from the end, so output order is reversed. (2) Deeply nested closures get their names qualified one level at a time, because the renamed block is pushed back on the stack. (3) Methods of a renamed class are appended separately, and their own names are not prefixed.

79	    '''Process a list of blocks by adding all closures and inner classes as
80	    top-level blocks.

82	    new_blocks = []
83	    all_blocks = blocks[:]
84	    while all_blocks:
